vulnerability.name: Erlang Distribution Guessable Cookie RCE
vulnerability.author: SecGen Pipeline
vulnerability.description: A distributed Erlang node is running on the host with a weak, guessable distribution cookie. Erlang distribution trusts any peer that presents the correct cookie: the shared secret is the only authentication. Once an attacker knows (or brute-forces) the cookie they can speak the distribution protocol directly to the node's listener and issue an rpc call, turning os:cmd into arbitrary command execution as the account running the node. The node runs as an unprivileged service user, so the shell lands as that user. The teaching point is that an Erlang cookie is a password: leaking it, or leaving the default/weak one, gives remote code execution. This is the distribution-cookie weakness, not the Erlang/OTP SSH daemon CVE (see ssh/ssh_erlangotp_rce for that). The Metasploit module exploit/multi/misc/erlang_cookie_rce automates it.
vulnerability.hint: A distributed Erlang node with a weak distribution cookie, reachable over the network (epmd on 4369 and a distribution listener on a high port)
vulnerability.solution: Treat the Erlang cookie as a secret: use a long random cookie, keep ~/.erlang.cookie mode 0400, bind epmd and the distribution listener to trusted interfaces only, and never ship a default or dictionary-word cookie.
